verdict.root_cause: checkoutservice is failing a minority of PlaceOrder requests because a synchronous downstream call inside PlaceOrder stopped completing, not because of anything wrong in its own artifact or config. Its logs show intake continuing at a steady cadence with well-formed requests, but from 07:43:42 order-start entries are no longer followed by the payment/confirmation/queue-write completions that accompanied every start in the healthy baseline, so requests hang at or before the payment step [tr_7bebc6f2bf4e]. The error ratio steps from ~1.5% to ~3.9% with peaks near 28% and one change point at 07:41:45 - partial degradation consistent with timeouts on a slow dependency rather than a crash or hard outage [tr_c5f5bea387ac]. No checkoutservice change exists in the window [tr_0bb613f4937e], and the only nearby change activity is an automated fault-injection harness on cartservice whose latency sidecar, hotfix image and REDIS_ADDR override were all reverted 1.6-2.2h before onset [tr_2b5e71e89dd5]. The specific slow downstream is not identified by the dispatches performed.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent signals agree the failure is a wait, not a defect in checkoutservice itself: no change record for checkoutservice, no error-severity log lines, and a partial (not total) error ratio with a sharp change point at 07:41:45. The log signature - starts without their usual completion trio, truncating at or before the payment-success entry - places the stall in a synchronous downstream call. The late-alerting peers (frontend, accounting, email, fraud, quote at 07:45-07:46) are consistent with propagation outward from checkout rather than independent faults. paymentservice could not be confirmed or cleared because its error-ratio series is empty in both windows [tr_41901647c03a], and cartservice's injected latency was demonstrably not live at onset [tr_2b5e71e89dd5], so the identity of the slow dependency remains open.
open_questions: Which downstream is slow: no trace-level or callee-side latency evidence was gathered for paymentservice, cartservice, currencyservice or shippingservice.
paymentservice has no error-ratio samples in either window - instrumentation gap, so its health is genuinely unknown.
The checkoutservice log result was silently truncated (07:13:50-07:43:42 unobserved) and the change query started at onset, so a change or error just before 07:41:45 is not excluded.
Whether the cartservice fault-injection harness fired again near 07:41:45 in a way the change log did not record.

alternatives.root_cause: The automated fault-injection harness on cartservice re-applied its egress-delay sidecar near 07:41:45, making checkout's cart call slow.
alternatives.why_not: The change log covering through 07:47 shows a 1.6h quiet period before onset and all three injected mutations already reverted, so no injection was live at onset.

alternatives.root_cause: paymentservice became slow or unresponsive, stalling checkout at the payment step.
alternatives.why_not: Its error-ratio series is empty in both incident and baseline windows, so nothing positively implicates it; the log stall is only bounded as 'at or before' payment.

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no effect should be observed. The condition that would justify acting is not yet observable: the stalled downstream inside PlaceOrder is unnamed. Concretely, before any action is taken this system should obtain (a) callee-side latency or error series for paymentservice, cartservice, currencyservice and shippingservice around 07:41:45, and (b) an untruncated checkoutservice log query over 07:13:50-07:43:42 plus a change query starting at least 30 minutes before 07:41:45. Only when one of those names a specific slow callee, with a change or process-state signal on it, does any permitted action have its preconditions met.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if the missing evidence would have been cheap and the incident is actively burning orders: ~3.9% mean and ~27.8% peak PlaceOrder error ratio persisting [tr_c5f5bea387ac] is real customer harm, and waiting has a cost. It would also be shown wrong if a targeted dispatch quickly reveals, say, a cartservice fault-injection sidecar still attached at 07:41:45 that the change log did not record - in which case revert_config on cartservice becomes the correct proposal and this abstention delayed it. Falsifier for the abstention's premise: any trace-level or callee-side latency evidence naming a single slow downstream would immediately supersede it.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is continued partial order failure with no mitigation. The risk of the actions I am declining is worse and is why I decline them: restart_service on checkoutservice is contraindicated because the process is demonstrably alive and accepting traffic at a steady cadence through 07:46:53 [tr_7bebc6f2bf4e], so a recreate would drop in-flight orders and in-process cache, is irreversible, and would not touch a downstream stall - it would also destroy the log continuity needed to identify the real callee. rollback_image on checkoutservice fails its precondition outright: the change log records nothing for checkoutservice in the window [tr_0bb613f4937e], so there is no prior tag the incident's evidence names. revert_config on cartservice fails its precondition too: all three harness mutations (image, latency sidecar, REDIS_ADDR) were already reverted 1.6-2.2h before onset [tr_2b5e71e89dd5], so 'reverting' would either be a no-op or would re-apply harness state and inject the very latency suspected. scale_service is unavailable in this world. Acting on a low-confidence verdict with an unidentified target risks recreating a healthy service and converting a 4% degradation into a full outage for the duration of the recreate.
proposal.blast_radius: None from this proposal, since nothing changes. For context on what is being declined: any action on checkoutservice would be seen by frontend (its caller) and propagate to loadgenerator, and would affect its synchronous downstreams cartservice, productcatalogservice, currencyservice, paymentservice, plus the async consumers accountingservice, emailservice, frauddetectionservice. Any action on cartservice would be seen by checkoutservice and, through it, the same set. The currently degraded population - a minority of PlaceOrder requests - remains degraded while evidence is gathered, and quoteservice/shippingservice remain affected as reported.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical multi-service failure fanning out from checkoutservice within minutes, touching downstream consumers and frontend; nothing here can be dismissed as a working system. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the alerts alone don't distinguish a deploy, config, or dependency cause.
